entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0478: Vulnerability in openssl
entry.summary: Unchecked callback lengths in PSK and cookie callbacks
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0478

Unchecked callback lengths in PSK and cookie callbacks
Reported
April 19, 2026
Issued
November 10, 2026
Package
openssl (crates.io)
Type
Vulnerability
Categories
  • memory-exposure
Keywords
#ssl #psk #dtls #cookie #out-of-bounds-read
Aliases
  • CVE-2026-41898
  • GHSA-hppc-g8h3-xhp3
References
  • https://github.com/rust-openssl/rust-openssl/pull/2607
Patched
  • >=0.10.78
Unaffected
  • <0.9.24
Affected Functions
Version
openssl::ssl::SslContextBuilder::set_cookie_generate_cb
  • >=0.9.24, <0.10.78
openssl::ssl::SslContextBuilder::set_psk_callback
  • >=0.9.24, <0.10.78
openssl::ssl::SslContextBuilder::set_psk_client_callback
  • >=0.9.24, <0.10.78
openssl::ssl::SslContextBuilder::set_psk_server_callback
  • >=0.9.24, <0.10.78
openssl::ssl::SslContextBuilder::set_stateless_cookie_generate_cb
  • >=0.9.24, <0.10.78

Description

The callbacks installed with SslContextBuilder::set_psk_client_callback (and its deprecated alias set_psk_callback), set_psk_server_callback, set_cookie_generate_cb and set_stateless_cookie_generate_cb each fill a &mut [u8] buffer and return how many bytes they wrote. The FFI trampolines handed that returned length straight to OpenSSL without checking it against the size of the buffer.

A callback that returns a length larger than its buffer makes OpenSSL read past the end of the buffer. For the cookie callbacks the cookie is sent to the peer, so adjacent memory can be disclosed over the network.

0.10.78 compares the returned length with the buffer size and treats a larger value as a callback failure.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0474: Vulnerability in openssl
entry.summary: `X509Ref::ocsp_responders` can produce a `&str` that is not valid UTF-8
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0474

X509Ref::ocsp_responders can produce a &str that is not valid UTF-8
Reported
May 4, 2026
Issued
November 10, 2026
Package
openssl (crates.io)
Type
Vulnerability
Keywords
#x509 #ocsp #utf-8 #undefined-behavior
Aliases
  • CVE-2026-42327
  • GHSA-xp3w-r5p5-63rr
References
  • https://github.com/rust-openssl/rust-openssl/pull/2631
Patched
  • >=0.10.79
Unaffected
  • <0.9.7
Affected Functions
Version
openssl::x509::X509Ref::ocsp_responders
  • >=0.9.7, <0.10.79

Description

X509Ref::ocsp_responders returns the OCSP responder URLs from a certificate's Authority Information Access extension as OpensslString values, which dereference to str without validating the bytes. OpenSSL does not require these IA5String values to be ASCII, so for a certificate with non-UTF-8 bytes in an OCSP access location, safe code ends up holding a &str that is not valid UTF-8, which is undefined behavior. Certificates often come from untrusted peers.

ocsp_responders was added in 0.9.7. 0.10.79 checks each URL and returns an error if it is not valid UTF-8.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0479: Vulnerability in openssl
entry.summary: Out-of-bounds read when a PEM password callback returns an oversized length
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0479

Out-of-bounds read when a PEM password callback returns an oversized length
Reported
April 19, 2026
Issued
November 10, 2026
Package
openssl (crates.io)
Type
Vulnerability
Categories
  • memory-exposure
Keywords
#pem #password #callback #out-of-bounds-read
Aliases
  • CVE-2026-41677
  • GHSA-xmgf-hq76-4vx2
References
  • https://github.com/rust-openssl/rust-openssl/pull/2605
Patched
  • >=0.10.78
Unaffected
  • <0.9.0

Description

The *_from_pem_callback functions, such as EcKey::private_key_from_pem_callback, pass the length returned by the user's password callback to OpenSSL without checking it against the size of the buffer the callback was given. If the callback reports more bytes than the buffer holds, some OpenSSL versions read past the end of the buffer while deriving the decryption key. OpenSSL 3.x is not affected.

0.10.78 treats a returned length larger than the buffer as a failed callback.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

entry.summary: Buffer overflow with AES key wrap with padding in `cipher_update_inplace`
entry.content:

RUSTSEC-2026-0477

Buffer overflow with AES key wrap with padding in cipher_update_inplace
Reported

Issued

Package
openssl (crates.io)
Type
Vulnerability
Categories
  • memory-corruption
Keywords
#aes #key-wrap #cipher #buffer-overflow
Aliases
  • CVE-2026-45784
  • GHSA-phqj-4mhp-q6mq
References
  • https://github.com/rust-openssl/rust-openssl/pull/2638
Patched
  • >=0.10.80
Unaffected
  • <0.10.50
Affected Functions
Version
openssl::cipher_ctx::CipherCtxRef::cipher_update_inplace
  • >=0.10.50, <0.10.80

Description

CipherCtxRef::cipher_update_inplace had the same sizing error that 0.10.79 fixed in cipher_update (GHSA-xv59-967r-8726); that fix missed this method. It required room for inlen + block_size bytes, but with the AES key-wrap-with-padding ciphers OpenSSL writes up to 7 more bytes when inlen is not a multiple of 8, past the end of data.

Only users of the AES key-wrap-with-padding ciphers are affected. cipher_update_inplace was added in 0.10.50, and 0.10.80 applies the corrected size check to it.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0475: Vulnerability in openssl
entry.summary: Buffer overflow in `MdCtxRef::digest_final`
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0475

Buffer overflow in MdCtxRef::digest_final
Reported
April 19, 2026
Issued
November 10, 2026
Package
openssl (crates.io)
Type
Vulnerability
Categories
  • memory-corruption
Keywords
#digest #buffer-overflow
Aliases
  • CVE-2026-41681
  • GHSA-ghm9-cr32-g9qj
References
  • https://github.com/rust-openssl/rust-openssl/pull/2608
Patched
  • >=0.10.78
Unaffected
  • <0.10.39
Affected Functions
Version
openssl::md_ctx::MdCtxRef::digest_final
  • >=0.10.39, <0.10.78

Description

MdCtxRef::digest_final passed the caller's output slice to OpenSSL's EVP_DigestFinal without checking its length. EVP_DigestFinal always writes the full digest (EVP_MD_CTX_size bytes), so an output slice shorter than the digest is overrun. With a stack buffer this usually corrupts the stack. The overflow is reachable from safe code.

MdCtxRef was added in 0.10.39. 0.10.78 checks the slice length first and returns an error when the slice is too short for the digest.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0476: Vulnerability in openssl
entry.summary: Buffer overflow with AES key wrap with padding in `cipher_update`
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0476

Buffer overflow with AES key wrap with padding in cipher_update
Reported
May 4, 2026
Issued
November 10, 2026
Package
openssl (crates.io)
Type
Vulnerability
Categories
  • memory-corruption
Keywords
#aes #key-wrap #cipher #buffer-overflow
Aliases
  • CVE-2026-44662
  • GHSA-xv59-967r-8726
References
  • https://github.com/rust-openssl/rust-openssl/pull/2630
Patched
  • >=0.10.79
Unaffected
  • <0.10.0
Affected Functions
Version
openssl::cipher_ctx::CipherCtxRef::cipher_update
  • >=0.10.0, <0.10.79
openssl::cipher_ctx::CipherCtxRef::cipher_update_vec
  • >=0.10.0, <0.10.79
openssl::symm::Crypter::update
  • >=0.10.0, <0.10.79

Description

CipherCtxRef::cipher_update, CipherCtxRef::cipher_update_vec and symm::Crypter::update require (or allocate) input.len() + block_size bytes of output. With the AES key-wrap-with-padding ciphers (EVP_aes_128_wrap_pad, EVP_aes_192_wrap_pad, EVP_aes_256_wrap_pad), OpenSSL pads the input to a multiple of 8 bytes and adds an 8-byte block, so when the input length is not a multiple of 8 it writes up to 7 bytes past the end of the caller's buffer or Vec. If an attacker can influence the plaintext length, this is heap corruption they can partly control.

Only users of the AES key-wrap-with-padding ciphers are affected. 0.10.79 sizes the output for these ciphers as the input length rounded up to a multiple of 8, plus 8.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0473: Vulnerability in openssl
entry.summary: Buffer overflow in `Deriver::derive` and `PkeyCtxRef::derive` with OpenSSL 1.1.x
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0473

Buffer overflow in Deriver::derive and PkeyCtxRef::derive with OpenSSL 1.1.x
Reported
April 19, 2026
Issued
November 10, 2026
Package
openssl (crates.io)
Type
Vulnerability
Categories
  • memory-corruption
Keywords
#derive #x25519 #x448 #hkdf #buffer-overflow
Aliases
  • CVE-2026-41676
  • GHSA-pqf5-4pqq-29f5
References
  • https://github.com/rust-openssl/rust-openssl/pull/2606
Patched
  • >=0.10.78
Unaffected
  • <0.9.27
Affected Functions
Version
openssl::derive::Deriver::derive
  • >=0.9.27, <0.10.78
openssl::pkey_ctx::PkeyCtxRef::derive
  • >=0.9.27, <0.10.78

Description

Deriver::derive and PkeyCtxRef::derive pass the length of the caller's buffer to EVP_PKEY_derive and rely on OpenSSL to write no more than that. With OpenSSL 1.1.x, the X25519, X448 and HKDF-extract implementations ignore the length they are given and always write the whole result, so a buffer shorter than the shared secret or derived key is overrun. The overflow is reachable from safe code.

OpenSSL 3.x checks the length itself and is not affected. From 0.10.78, when built against OpenSSL 1.1.x or LibreSSL, both functions derive into a temporary buffer of the required size whenever the caller's buffer is too short, and copy only what fits.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0463: Vulnerability in openssl
entry.summary: Out-of-bounds write in `aes::unwrap_key`
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0463

Out-of-bounds write in aes::unwrap_key
Reported
April 19, 2026
Issued
November 9, 2026
Package
openssl (crates.io)
Type
Vulnerability
Categories
  • memory-corruption
Keywords
#aes #key-wrap #out-of-bounds-write
Aliases
  • CVE-2026-41678
  • GHSA-8c75-8mhr-p7r9
References
  • https://github.com/rust-openssl/rust-openssl/pull/2604
Patched
  • >=0.10.78
Unaffected
  • <0.10.24
Affected Functions
Version
openssl::aes::unwrap_key
  • >=0.10.24, <0.10.78

Description

openssl::aes::unwrap_key guarded the size of its output buffer with an inverted assertion, out.len() + 8 <= in_.len(). Instead of rejecting an out buffer too small for the unwrapped key, it rejected buffers larger than needed and accepted buffers that were too small.

When out is shorter than in_.len() - 8 bytes, the underlying AES_unwrap_key call writes past the end of out. This out-of-bounds write is reachable from a safe function; applications that let untrusted input influence the input or output buffer sizes are exposed.

The function was added in 0.10.24. 0.10.78 corrects the assertion, so an output buffer that is too small now causes a panic before anything is written.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0456: Vulnerability in heifer-hevc-dec
entry.summary: Panic on an HEVC tile layout that does not match the active SPS
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0456

Panic on an HEVC tile layout that does not match the active SPS
Reported
November 4, 2026
Issued
November 9, 2026
Package
heifer-hevc-dec (crates.io)
Type
Vulnerability
Categories
  • denial-of-service
Keywords
#hevc #h265 #heic #panic
Aliases
  • GHSA-rcff-5x58-7w2p
References
  • https://github.com/HarpeLm/Heifer/commit/71dfc67f1e3ae3c4b7e4cf633e83a26c94b06a92
CVSS Score
6.5 MEDIUM
CVSS Details
Attack Vector
Network
Attack Complexity
Low
Privileges Required
None
User Interaction
Required
Scope
Unchanged
Confidentiality Impact
None
Integrity Impact
None
Availability Impact
High
CVSS Vector
CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H
Patched
  • >=0.3.27

Description

An HEVC picture parameter set (PPS) stores explicit tile column widths and row heights computed against the sequence parameter set (SPS) active when it was parsed. A crafted stream can redefine that SPS afterwards, so that the tile sizes add up to more than the picture. The decoder then indexed past its coding tree block tables: Rust's bounds checks turned this into a panic, or the picture was decoded wrongly. A panic aborts the decoding thread, or the whole process when built with panic = "abort". The crate forbids unsafe code, so there is no memory corruption.

Any application that decodes untrusted HEIC files or HEVC streams with heifer-hevc-dec, directly or through the heifer crate, is affected.

The flaw was corrected in 0.3.27 (commit 71dfc67): a tile layout that does not match the picture size is rejected with Error::Invalid at decode time.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0461: Vulnerability in rmcp
entry.summary: Unbounded tool schema cache in Streamable HTTP server transport
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0461

Unbounded tool schema cache in Streamable HTTP server transport
Reported
October 20, 2026
Issued
November 9, 2026
Package
rmcp (crates.io)
Type
Vulnerability
Categories
  • denial-of-service
Keywords
#mcp #http #memory-exhaustion
Aliases
  • GHSA-4432-vg92-fqh6
References
  • https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk/pull/1349
CVSS Score
7.5 HIGH
CVSS Details
Attack Vector
Network
Attack Complexity
Low
Privileges Required
None
User Interaction
None
Scope
Unchanged
Confidentiality Impact
None
Integrity Impact
None
Availability Impact
High
CVSS Vector
CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H
Patched
  • >=3.6.0
Unaffected
  • <3.0.0

Description

From 3.0.0 until 3.6.0, StreamableHttpService cached the result of ServerHandler::get_tool in a process-wide map keyed by the tool name of incoming tools/call requests. The map had no size limit and no eviction, and it also cached unknown tool names.

An entry was added while the request headers were validated, before the request could be rejected, so requests answered with HTTP 400 still grew the map. A client that can reach the endpoint can send tools/call requests with distinct tool names, each up to the default 4 MiB body limit, until the server runs out of memory. rmcp does not authenticate requests itself, so servers without an authentication layer in front of the endpoint are exposed to unauthenticated clients.

Only servers that use the Streamable HTTP server transport and receive requests at protocol version 2026-07-28 or later are affected.

The flaw was corrected in 3.6.0 by removing the cache. The transport now calls ServerHandler::get_tool on each request.

If you cannot upgrade, put authentication in front of the endpoint, or reject tools/call requests for unknown tool names before they reach StreamableHttpService.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.

Related
  • GHSA-c9xm-49cp-xcr9
Patched
  • >=3.7.0
Unaffected
  • <2.0.0

Description

From 2.0.0 until 3.7.0, the rmcp OAuth client decided whether it may fetch an authorization server's metadata URL by inspecting only the host string. It rejected literal loopback, private and link-local IP addresses and known cloud metadata hostnames, but it did not resolve other hostnames. A hostname that resolves to an internal address passed the check.

A malicious MCP server can return protected-resource metadata that names an authorization server whose hostname resolves to an internal address. The client then sends GET requests to that address during discovery.

The same release fixes two related bypasses:

  • Bracketed IPv6 literals such as http://[::1]:6379/ were not recognized as internal, because the check kept the brackets from the URL host.
  • token_endpoint and registration_endpoint from authorization server metadata were not checked at all, and token requests follow redirects. A malicious authorization server could make the client send POST requests to an internal address.

The impact is client-side SSRF. Responses are not returned to the attacker directly. Unauthenticated internal HTTP services are reachable. Cloud metadata endpoints that require headers or IMDSv2 are largely unaffected.

The flaw was corrected in 3.7.0. AuthorizationManager::new now builds its HTTP client with a DNS resolver that applies the address policy to every resolved address, and checks every IP-literal URL and followed redirect against the same policy. Loopback and private addresses are allowed only when the MCP server's own URL names one of that class. Deployments that reach their authorization server through a hostname that resolves to a private address should use AuthorizationManager::new_allowing_private_addresses.

Clients supplied through new_with_oauth_http_client are not covered by the resolved-address checks. Such clients must enforce their own outbound address policy.

Description

Before 3.9.0, the built-in Streamable HTTP clients in rmcp read non-streaming HTTP response bodies into memory with no size limit. Both the reqwest client (transport-streamable-http-client-reqwest) and the Unix socket client (transport-streamable-http-client-unix-socket) were affected:

  • application/json responses to POST requests were read in full before parsing.
  • Non-2xx responses were read in full for error reporting.

A malicious or compromised MCP server can answer with a body that never ends, for example a chunked application/json response that streams whitespace. The client buffers it until the process runs out of memory. This works during initialize, before any authentication. On desktop or agent hosts, this terminates the whole host application.

Server-sent event streams are not affected. Each event is already capped by max_sse_event_size, and events are not accumulated.

The flaw was corrected in 3.9.0. Successful JSON bodies are limited to 16 MiB and non-success bodies to 64 KiB. Bytes are counted while streaming, after decompression. An oversized Content-Length is rejected before the body is read, and an oversized body is rejected with StreamableHttpError::ResponseBodyTooLarge instead of being truncated.

If you cannot upgrade, use a custom StreamableHttpClient that enforces a response body limit, or connect only to trusted MCP servers.

SQLite versions before 3.54.0 can return uninitialized page-cache memory when a process opens a database file together with a sibling write-ahead-log (-wal) file whose page size differs from the database's. A crafted pair of files can make ordinary queries return stale bytes from the process's memory. The attack vector is local and needs the victim to open the files.

Only a process that opens a database file, with its -wal, that a less trusted party could have written is exposed. A build that links a system SQLite instead of the bundled source is not affected by the copy in this crate; its exposure is that of the system library's version. The bundled-sqlcipher feature builds SQLCipher instead of SQLite; in 0.39.0 and 0.39.1 it depends on sqlcipher-src =419.0.6, which bundles SQLite 3.53.4 and is affected.

Description

InternalKeyRef::from_encoded is a safe constructor whose only length check is debug_assert!(encoded.len() >= 16), which is compiled out in release builds. Its accessors perform unchecked length arithmetic on the slice: user_key() slices &encoded[..len - 16], trailer()/seq_num() pass len - 16 and timestamp() passes len - 8 to read_u64_be, which computes buffer.as_ptr().add(offset) and performs an 8-byte load. For a short slice the subtraction underflows usize, the pointer wraps below the allocation and eight bytes before the buffer are read (undefined behavior; confirmed with AddressSanitizer as a heap-buffer-overflow). In debug builds the same call panics instead.

The same invariant is missing at the on-disk decode boundary: BlockIterator::seek_next_entry rebuilds the current key from block bytes with upper-bound checks only, and BlockIterator::key() wraps it in InternalKeyRef, which surrealdb's kv-surrealkv backend then reads through key_ref.timestamp(). A crafted or corrupted SSTable therefore reaches the same unchecked subtraction without any unsafe at the call site.

1.2.0 rejects internal keys shorter than their 8-byte trailer before any accessor computes an offset and makes the accessors bounds-checked (fix in commit ac642f9, surrealdb 4.0.0 ships surrealkv 1.2.0).

Description

The kv-mem, kv-surrealkv and kv-rocksdb backends move non-'static borrowed state into affinity-pool closures through affinitypool::spawn_local: a tokio::sync::MutexGuard<Option<TransactionInner>>, &Transaction, &mut ScanStateKeys/Vals, &mut dyn KeyVisitor/ValVisitor, RwLockReadGuard, and a ReadOptions holding a raw rocksdb_snapshot_t*. In affinitypool 0.7.0 spawn_local is safe and erases the 'pool lifetime via async_task::Builder::spawn_unchecked; the only thing keeping it sound is the Drop implementation of the returned future, which blocks until the worker stops using the borrows.

Safe code can leak that future (mem::forget, Box::leak, ManuallyDrop, a reference cycle, or a leaked enclosing future). The borrows then end while the pool worker still uses them, producing a use-after-free on the transaction allocation; AddressSanitizer reports a read of freed mutex data and a write when the worker unlocks the freed tokio::sync::Mutex on the pool thread. No unsafe is required at the call site, and the affected methods include count, keys/keysr, scan/scanr, compact, shutdown, point reads and writes, and cursor iteration.

3.3.0 upgrades to affinitypool 0.8.0, where spawn_local is an unsafe function and the caller must uphold the leak-freedom invariant (commit 8156ff69).

Description

dbs::Executor drives every SurrealQL statement through reblessive::tree::TreeStack. In reblessive 0.4.3 the runtime types unconditionally assert Send/Sync (unsafe impl Send/Sync for Stack, TreeStack and Runner), while the public entry points accept any future without a Send bound and store it type-erased in a bump allocator.

Two safe-code consequences follow. First, Runner::step_async/finish_async return driver futures tied to the stack borrow rather than to &mut self, so a driver future can be duplicated; because Stack is Sync those futures are Send, and polling two copies on different threads runs drive_top_task concurrently — racy Cell/UnsafeCell access, double pop_task()/pop_dealloc() (double drop / double free) and a non-atomic Option::take. Second, TreeStack: Send lets safe code move a driver whose type-erased future captures !Send state (Rc, RefCell) to another thread while the creating thread keeps an alias of that state.

No unsafe is needed at the call site. surrealdb-core's own query futures are Send only because of the unsound unsafe impl Send for TreeStack, while the captured &mut tree::Stk is deliberately !Send.

The unsound dependency was removed in 4.0.0 and the parser now uses plain recursion (commit 75407c4bcc).

  • For ocipkg-specific functionality (local package management, or build-time library fetching and linking), the maintainer suggests forking the repository from 0.4.1 and maintaining it for your use case, as oci-client is not a drop-in replacement for those features.

RUSTSEC-2026-0450

ocipkg: unpacking an OCI archive can write and delete files outside the local image store (path traversal)

CVSS Vector
CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:H
Patched
  • >=0.4.1
Affected Functions
Version
ocipkg::image::load
  • <=0.4.0

Description

When ocipkg unpacks an OCI archive, the destination directory is derived from the image name, which ocipkg reads from the archive's own index.json (org.opencontainers.image.ref.name). That name is attacker-controlled, and ImageName::parse accepts a hostname of .., so the computed destination escapes the local image store. A "zip-slip"-style path traversal (CWE-22 / CWE-23). This is esclatable to code execution.

In Artifact::unpack (src/image/artifact.rs), the destination is image_dir(name) = data_dir().join(name.as_path()) (src/local/mod.rs:31), where the name comes from get_name_from_index (src/image/layout.rs:114-124):

let image_name = self.base.get_name()?;   // from the archive's index.json ref.name
let dest = image_dir(&image_name)?;        // data_dir().join(name.as_path()); hostname ".." escapes
if dest.exists() {
    if overwrite {
        fs::remove_dir_all(&dest)?;        // deletes a directory OUTSIDE the store
    }
}
fs::create_dir_all(&dest)?;
// ... each tar layer is then unpacked under `dest` (also outside the store)

The fix

Fixed in ocipkg 0.4.1 by PR #223. The leading reference component is validated against the org.opencontainers.image.ref.name grammar from OCI Image Specification 1.1.1 on parse and deserialization, and local::image_dir revalidates the name and rejects any non-normal path component (e.g. ..) before any filesystem mutation, so a crafted archive can no longer escape the local image store.

Description

Improper validation of RunEndEncoded arrays via ArrayData::validate_values can allow reading data beyond the bounds of the child values array when reading the last value via APIs such as TypedRunArray::value.

entry.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0437: Vulnerability in azure_security_keyvault_certificates
entry.summary: Rejected authentication challenges can poison the Key Vault scope cache
entry.content:
History ⋅ Edit ⋅ JSON (OSV)

RUSTSEC-2026-0437

Rejected authentication challenges can poison the Key Vault scope cache
Reported
August 24, 2026
Issued
November 5, 2026
Package
azure_security_keyvault_certificates (crates.io)
Type
Vulnerability
Keywords
#keyvault #authentication #challenge #cache
References
  • https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-rust/pull/5121
  • https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-rust/pull/5125
  • https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-rust/pull/5410
Patched
  • >=1.0.1, <1.1.0-beta.0
  • >=1.1.0-beta.2
Unaffected
  • <0.9.0

Description

Affected versions of KeyVaultAuthorizer::on_challenge cache the authentication scope from a WWW-Authenticate response before verifying that the challenge resource matches the requested endpoint. When verification rejects the challenge, the scope remains cached. A subsequent request through the same client uses that scope to authorize the request without repeating challenge resource verification.

For azure_security_keyvault_certificates, the affected versions are 0.9.0 through 1.0.0, inclusive, and 1.1.0-beta.1. Versions before 0.9.0 do not use this challenge-scope cache and are unaffected by this issue.

Impact

An application that sends requests to an attacker-controlled endpoint and reuses the same client after a rejected challenge can disclose a bearer token and request body to that endpoint, if its credential can obtain a token for the supplied scope. The first request's validation error therefore does not prevent disclosure on a later request. Changing the request origin between requests is not required.

Fix

Update to 1.0.1 on the stable release line or 1.1.0-beta.2 on the preview release line.

The fix caches the scope only after challenge resource verification succeeds when verification is enabled. Rejected challenges no longer populate the cache. The existing option to disable challenge resource verification is unchanged; this fix does not add exact-origin binding.

Advisory available under CC0-1.0 license.
